entries.test: Whether AI makes cures for most human diseases possible by August 2036.
entries.note: The title and subsequent categorical rejection support reading this as a negative forecast.

entries.test: Drug approval records and documented clinical use would establish whether any AI-designed drug had reached clinical adoption by March 2026.
entries.note: Marcus explicitly attributes the observation to Javorsky, while adopting it as a premise.

entries.test: Public drug-development records and regulatory requirements would establish the economic, technical, and clinical-validation constraints that persist for AI-designed treatments.
entries.note: This states continuing constraints on developing cures rather than identifying a causal relationship. The hypothetical improvement in AI does not remove the concrete claim about required clinical work.
Neither the requisite causal and biological sophistication nor what would fundamentally change the argument has a shared operational threshold.

entries.test: Public reactions to Amodei's August 2026 remarks, compared with reactions to earlier similar predictions, would show whether substantial pushback emerged.
entries.note: The surrounding examples give the mood claim a concrete reading: increased public criticism of these cure timelines.

entries.test: Hassabis's referenced 60 Minutes remarks and documented medical outcomes through August 2036 would establish whether AI delivered the disease-curing advances he described.
entries.note: The next-decade exclusion is categorical despite the concession that contributions might occur someday. Its scope is the referenced cure projections.

entries.test: AI companies' public disclosures before the post would establish whether any presented a concrete plan to cure a specified disease within five to ten years.
entries.note: “As far as I know” qualifies an assertion about public plans; it does not turn it into a prediction of mere possibility.
Calling Amodei's repeated promises “unrealistic hope” expresses an evaluative judgment without a defined standard.
This is a conditional recommendation to undertake medical training.
